  > PSI-119, the pure CPM/PERT engine, built test-first as the brief's §4 lane assigns. Added src/features/schedule/lib/pert.ts (computeSchedule, targetProbability, sigmaRange, slackBand and the PertTask/TaskLink/NodeResult/Schedule/ScheduleError types exactly as cpm-evm.md -> PSI-119 fixes them) and src/features/schedule/lib/normal-cdf.ts (Abramowitz & Stegun 7.1.26 erf, |error| < 1.5e-7, no dependency), with 23 unit tests in pert.test.ts. The brief's 38-week fixture reproduces exactly: A ES 0 EF 8, B 8-18, C 8-14 slack 4, D 18-31, E 31-35, critical path A-B-D-E, TE 35 w, variance 8.667 w^2, sigma 2.944 w, z(38) 1.019, P 0.846, 2-sigma range 29.112-40.888 w. Also covered: a cycle (including a one-node self-link), a link to an id with no estimate, estimates breaking 0 <= a <= m <= b (a>m, m>b, negative, NaN, Infinity), an empty network, a zero-duration milestone, zero sigma, two equal-length critical paths, a fan-in, an unlinked task, input immutability and a purity guard that greps the module for new Date/Date.now/Math.random. Two things worth flagging rather than hiding: (1) the card's accept line says 'path TE and sigma as sums along the critical path', but the brief's glossary and the fixture define project sigma as the SQUARE ROOT of the summed variances - I implemented the glossary/fixture (variance sums to 8.667 w^2, sigma is 2.944 w) and recorded the wording clash as a follow-up, because the card as written would have you sum sigmas to 7.0 w; (2) on a duration tie the reported critical path is the one carrying the larger variance, so a task with zero slack that is not on that path still reports critical: true - correct CPM, but PSI-120 must not treat the boolean as membership in criticalPath. No React, no Date, no I/O, no new dependency. PSI-120/PSI-121 consume this module; nothing else imports it yet.
